segments.text: The campus library recently introduced a policy that treats a first late return far more gently than before. A

, since the fee simply disappears instead of being charged. This result gets logged quietly on the account, so staff can spot a pattern if it happens again. A second late return works differently: that same record gains a temporary hold, and no further items can be borrowed until the charge from that visit is settled.

gaps.explanationZh: 此處需要一個名詞作為子句主詞，指「借書逾期的人」。後文以 who 引導的關係子句描述其行為（brings a title back past its deadline），且與圖書館情境相符，故填入 student（學生）。
此處需要及物動詞，與主詞 A student（第三人稱單數）搭配現在式，並與後方 back 構成片語動詞 bring...back（歸還），故填入 brings，時態上也與同句稍後的 receives 一致。
此處需要名詞作為動詞 brings back 的受詞，指被歸還的物品。因主題是圖書館逾期還書政策，借閱物在圖書館語境中常稱為 title（書名／書籍），故填入 title。
此處需要介系詞，表示「超過期限」之意，與後方名詞 deadline 搭配構成 past its deadline（超過截止日），故填入 past。
此處需要名詞作為介系詞 past 的受詞，指還書的截止日期，與句意「逾期歸還」直接對應，故填入 deadline。
此處需要定冠詞，用於片語 for the very first time（第一次），因為此為特定、獨一無二的「第一次」概念，須用 the 而非不定冠詞，故填入 the。
此處需要序數詞，與 very 搭配構成強調語氣的 very first time（真正的第一次），呼應段首提到的「首次逾期」政策差異，故填入 first。
此處需要副詞，表示與「以前」（than before）相對的「現在」，凸顯新政策生效後的當下情況，與句首 recently introduced 及 far more gently than before 形成時間對比，故填入 now。
此處需要不定冠詞，置於以母音開頭的形容詞 automatic 之前，依英文文法須用 an 而非 a，故填入 an。
此處需要名詞，作為動詞 receives 的受詞，指學生獲得的處置結果。後文說明「fee simply disappears instead of being charged」，正是「被免除、獲得寬恕」之意，故填入 pardon（免罰／寬恕）。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: The campus library recently introduced a policy that treats a first late return far more gently than before. A student who brings a title back past its deadline for the very first time now receives an automatic pardon, since the fee simply disappears instead of being charged. This result gets logged quietly on the account, so staff can spot a pattern if it happens again. A second late return works differently: that same record gains a temporary hold, and no further items can be borrowed until the charge from that visit is settled.

segments.text: Many retail stores now train employees to work in more than one department instead of just one fixed role. Each

that someone besides the regular person can always cover a shift when a coworker is sick or away. Managers publish the upcoming schedule roughly seven days ahead, so every employee already knows which assignment they will support next.

gaps.explanationZh: 前方主詞是「Each」,表示指涉單一個體,後面應接單數名詞「worker」(員工),與動詞 spends 的單數主詞一致,語意上呼應前句提到每位員工被訓練支援多個部門。
「a short ___」需要一個可被 short 修飾的單數名詞,「period」(一段時間)符合語意,表示員工花一小段時間學習任務,且與後面的動名詞 learning 銜接自然。
動詞 learning 之後需要受詞,「tasks」(任務、工作項目)符合語境,指員工在不同部門學習的具體工作內容,且與前後複數用法一致。
「in a different ___」需要單數名詞作介系詞受詞,「section」(部門、區域)符合語意,呼應前句提到的 department,表示員工在不同區域學習任務。
「before ___ to another area」中 before 為介系詞,後面須接動名詞,「rotating」(輪調)符合語法與語意,表示學習完後接著輪調到另一個區域。
「to ___ area completely」需要限定詞修飾單數名詞 area,「another」(另一個)符合語意,表示員工完全輪調到另一個不同的工作區域。
「another area ___」需要副詞修飾整個輪調動作,「completely」(完全地)符合語意,強調員工是完全轉換到新的區域而非部分兼顧原區域。
句首「A ___ of this kind」需要單數名詞作主詞,「rotation」(輪調制度)呼應前文描述的員工輪流學習不同部門任務的做法,並與後面單數動詞 guarantees 一致。
「of ___ kind」需要指示詞修飾 kind,「this」(這種)符合語意,指涉前文剛描述過的輪調方式,屬於指示代名詞的典型用法。
主詞「A rotation of this kind」為單數,動詞須用第三人稱單數形式,「guarantees」(保證)符合語法,且語意上表示這種輪調制度確保總有人能代班。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: Many retail stores now train employees to work in more than one department instead of just one fixed role. Each worker spends a short period learning tasks in a different section before rotating to another area completely. A rotation of this kind guarantees that someone besides the regular person can always cover a shift when a coworker is sick or away. Managers publish the upcoming schedule roughly seven days ahead, so every employee already knows which assignment they will support next.

academic.title: Why Willpower Feels Different by Time of Day
academic.text:
Psychologists who study self-control have noticed a curious pattern: people often make sharper decisions in the morning than they do by late afternoon. One explanation centers on the sheer number of small choices a person makes across an ordinary day. Deciding what to wear, which email to answer first, or whether to skip a meeting all draw on the same limited mental resource. Even when each choice feels trivial, the cumulative effect can be considerable by the time evening arrives.

Researchers describe this decline as a gradual narrowing of attention rather than a sudden collapse. Without any pause for rest, judgment becomes noticeably less careful, and people tend to default to whichever option requires the least effort, regardless of whether it is the best one. A cashier might unconsciously round a bill in the customer's favor; a manager might approve a request simply to end a long meeting.

Interestingly, the effect is not permanent. A short break, even ten or fifteen minutes away from ongoing tasks, appears to restore much of the lost sharpness. Some workplaces have begun scheduling brief rest periods into the middle of the day for exactly this reason, treating attention less as a fixed trait and more as a resource that predictably rises and falls.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.text: A comparison of how offices schedule morning and afternoon meetings
The reason judgment typically weakens as the day progresses
The physical causes of fatigue following short mental tasks
The specific tasks that consume the most daily mental effort

questions.explanationZh: 全文說明判斷力如何隨著一天推移而逐漸減弱，此為文章核心主旨，其餘選項僅涉及次要或非重點內容。

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "cumulative" most likely mean?

options.text: reversed quickly by one action
sudden and unexpected in nature
occurring only one time
adding up little by little

questions.explanationZh: cumulative指效果隨時間逐漸累積疊加，而非單次、突然或可被單一動作逆轉，符合上下文描述決定持續累積的意涵。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about a manager who approves a request just to end a meeting?

options.text: The manager received formal training in delegation skills
The manager intends to undo the decision the next day
The manager's judgment has weakened from many earlier decisions
The manager privately disagrees but approves to be polite

questions.explanationZh: 文章指出經過多次選擇後判斷力下降，經理為求盡快結束會議而同意請求，可推知其判斷力已因先前決定而受影響。

questions.stem: How does the passage relate small daily decisions to the described decline in judgment?

options.text: It treats small decisions as the gradual cause of the decline
It claims the decline causes people to avoid making small decisions
It suggests the decline follows only one major daily decision
It argues the two developments merely happen to occur together

questions.explanationZh: 文章先描述一天中累積的大量小決定，再說明它們如何逐漸導致判斷力下降，呈現因果鋪陳的組織方式。

questions.stem: What is the purpose of mentioning workplaces that schedule brief rest periods?

options.text: To criticize companies for wasting employee time
To compare rest periods across different industries in detail
To illustrate a practical response some workplaces have adopted based on the described pattern
To argue that all breaks should last at least an hour

questions.explanationZh: 作者舉出安排休息時段的職場為例，說明這是根據前述現象所採取的實際因應做法。

ctwPassages.topic: shade trees as a climate cooling strategy for sidewalks

segments.text: City planners often plant shade trees along busy sidewalks to help cool hot pavement. A

a hot day. One with a wider canopy can cool a longer stretch of sidewalk. This simple method lowers cost while keeping streets more pleasant to walk on. Many towns now choose trees that grow quickly so shade arrives sooner.

gaps.explanationZh: 前一句已提到 planners 種植的是 shade trees，本句要指稱其中「一棵樹」擋住陽光，故單數主詞須填 tree，與後面单数動詞 blocks 一致。
句意是樹擋住「直射」的陽光才會在地面形成陰影降溫，所以要用 direct 修飾 sun，表示未經遮蔽、直接照射的陽光。
此處為固定搭配 block A from Ving，表示「阻止陽光照到地面」，故填 from，銜接後面的動名詞 hitting。
ground 指的是樹下那塊特定的地面（人行道路面），屬於上文已界定的特定對象，故須用定冠詞 the，而非泛指的 a。
樹遮蔭的位置是在樹「下方」的地面，below 表示位於樹冠之下，符合前句樹擋住陽光落在地面的空間關係。
本句新引入执行檢查工作的人，作句子主詞，且與後面動詞 check（無第三人稱單數 s）搭配，故用複數名詞 Workers。
主詞 Workers 為複數，動詞不加 s，且語意是工人「檢查」路面溫度，故填 check，與 often 副詞搭配的一般現在式動詞。
工人測量的是路面（人行道）表層的溫度，而非空氣溫度，故用 surface temperature 表示「表面溫度」。
此處表示檢查的時間大約在中午，並非精確時刻，故用 around noon 表示「大約中午時分」。
on a hot day 是固定的時間介系詞搭配，表示「在炎熱的一天」，用 on 銜接特定的一天。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: City planners often plant shade trees along busy sidewalks to help cool hot pavement. A tree blocks direct sun from hitting the ground below it. Workers often check the surface temperature around noon on a hot day. One with a wider canopy can cool a longer stretch of sidewalk. This simple method lowers cost while keeping streets more pleasant to walk on. Many towns now choose trees that grow quickly so shade arrives sooner.

academic.title: How Folk Music Instrument Makers Adapted to Modern Materials
academic.text:
For centuries, makers of traditional folk instruments used only wood, animal skin, and natural fiber. Today, many of these craftspeople blend synthetic materials into their instruments while still keeping much of the traditional wood. A guitar body might combine a solid wood top with a synthetic back panel, for example. This change did not happen quickly, and it did not happen without careful testing.

Before selling a new instrument, most makers compare its sound closely with an older, fully wooden version. They play both instruments side by side, listening for warmth, volume, and how long a note rings out. Only when the new version sounds close enough to the old one do makers consider the change successful. Many early attempts failed this test and were quietly abandoned.

One major reason for the shift is cost. Certain types of wood have become harder to find and far more expensive than they once were. Synthetic materials are more affordable and easier to shape consistently. By combining the two, makers can lower their prices without giving up the tone that customers expect. As a result, more people can afford a well-made instrument, and old musical traditions continue to reach new players.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what has caused certain types of wood to become expensive?

options.text: New environmental protection regulations imposed on all timber imports
A shortage of skilled woodworkers
Increased demand from furniture makers
The wood has become harder to find

questions.explanationZh: 原文提到特定木材becoming harder to find，導致成本上升，其餘原因（家具需求、進口法規、工匠短缺）原文皆未提及。

questions.stem: What does "abandoned" mean in the passage?

options.text: Sold at a discounted price
Given up and no longer pursued
Refined through several additional rounds of testing
Reported to industry regulators

questions.explanationZh: abandoned在此指嘗試失敗後被放棄，而非經多輪測試改良、降價出售或通報主管機關。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about an instrument that fails the sound comparison test?

options.text: It is still sold, but at a lower price
It is likely not released for sale
It is repaired using only synthetic material

questions.explanationZh: 原文指出通過測試才會被視為成功，可推知未通過音色比較的樂器通常不會上市銷售。

questions.stem: How does the passage organize its explanation of the change described?

options.text: It weighs two rival explanations for shrinking timber supplies before choosing one
It introduces a material change, then explains its testing and its cause
It ranks folk instruments by when each design was first invented
It outlines a lasting conflict between traditional and modern instrument makers

questions.explanationZh: 文章先介紹材質轉變，再說明如何測試音色是否合格，最後解釋成本為何促成此轉變，屬於先陳述現象、再解釋原因與驗證方式的組織方式。

questions.stem: Why does the passage mention that makers compare new instruments with fully wooden versions?

options.text: To illustrate how makers ensure the tone quality is preserved before adopting the change
To argue that synthetic materials always sound better
To explain a step required by government instrument-safety regulation
To show that fully wooden instruments are no longer being produced

questions.explanationZh: 作者提及與純木製樂器比較音色，用意在說明工匠如何確保改變材質後仍保留傳統音色品質。

ctwPassages.topic: a digital media platform's recommendation algorithm narrowing exposure

segments.text: Digital media platforms increasingly rely on recommendation engines that quietly reshape what each user later encounters online. Because

suggestions. Once this pattern takes hold, recommended options increasingly converge toward a single narrow category rather than reflecting broader interests. Consequently, unfamiliar genres and unexpected viewpoints surface far less often, even when a viewer might have genuinely valued them.

gaps.explanationZh: 此處填 earlier 修飾 clicks（點擊行為),表示「較早期的點擊」，並與後文 subsequent（後續的）建立時間對比，說明系統之所以能被早期行為左右，正是因為那些點擊發生在「較早」的時間點。
主詞 earlier clicks 為複數，需搭配動詞原形 carry（而非 carries）以符合主動詞一致；carry heavy influence 意為「帶有強大影響力」，銜接後面 inside the underlying system。
influence 作為 carry 的受詞（carry heavy influence），指「早期點擊在系統內部具有的影響力」，是整句「早期行為主導後續推薦」論點的關鍵名詞。
the 為定冠詞，用於修飾後面特定且前文已暗示的名詞 underlying system（推薦引擎背後運作的系統），指涉前一句提到的 recommendation engines，故需用定冠詞而非不定冠詞。
system 承接 the underlying，構成 the underlying system（底層運作的系統），呼應上一句 recommendation engines 背後的運作機制，是本句主要討論的對象。
handful 與 a...of 搭配構成片語 a handful of initial choices（少數幾個最初的選擇），強調只需極少數的早期選擇即可產生長期影響，符合全文「少量早期行為造成大範圍偏移」的論點。
initial 修飾 choices，意為「最初的選擇」，與前句 earlier clicks 語意呼應，同時與後文 subsequent suggestions 形成時間先後對比。
often 為副詞，修飾動詞 steers，表示「常常主導、影響」後續數月的建議內容，說明此現象並非偶發，而是具有一定頻率的普遍模式。
months 作為 steers 的受詞核心（months of subsequent suggestions），表示最初的選擇會左右「數個月」的後續推薦內容，凸顯影響時間之長。
subsequent 修飾 suggestions，意為「後續的建議」，與前文 earlier clicks、initial choices 形成時間對比，說明早期行為如何持續影響之後的推薦結果。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: Digital media platforms increasingly rely on recommendation engines that quietly reshape what each user later encounters online. Because earlier clicks carry heavy influence inside the underlying system, a handful of initial choices often steers months of subsequent suggestions. Once this pattern takes hold, recommended options increasingly converge toward a single narrow category rather than reflecting broader interests. Consequently, unfamiliar genres and unexpected viewpoints surface far less often, even when a viewer might have genuinely valued them.

academic.title: How Housing Cooperatives Pool Maintenance Costs
academic.text:
A housing cooperative differs from a conventional apartment building in that residents collectively own shares in the corporation that holds the property, rather than owning individual units outright. This structure creates a distinctive method for managing maintenance, one that spreads financial risk across the entire community of resident-owners rather than concentrating it on whoever happens to occupy a unit when a problem arises.

Each month, residents contribute a fixed amount into a shared reserve fund, calculated according to their proportional share in the cooperative. This contribution is deliberately kept separate from routine operating expenses such as utilities or staff wages. Over years, the reserve accumulates enough capital to absorb costly, infrequent repairs, a failing roof or an outdated elevator, without requiring a sudden, disruptive assessment charged to residents all at once.

Critics sometimes argue that this arrangement penalizes newer residents, who begin paying into a fund built partly for repairs that predate their arrival. Proponents counter that any resident, new or long-standing, ultimately benefits from a well-maintained building and predictable monthly costs, rather than facing an unpredictable emergency bill whenever a major system fails. Because the reserve is pooled rather than assigned to individual units, cooperatives can undertake major repairs promptly, without waiting for enough owners to agree to an unplanned, one-time payment.
